{
  "IP": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Shift operand and result data",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "The input word being shifted and the resulting shifted word are one data piece because the same shift operation transforms and returns it. The shifter's operation depends on this word, which enters through rs1_i and leaves through res_o.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The word can be exposed at res_o through lines 111 and 143, and its value can be altered by the internal data paths at lines 95, 99-101, 122, 128-129, 138, and 143.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe res_o or tamper with the operand or shift datapath so that the returned word reveals data or is incorrect.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "rs1_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "res_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        95,
        122,
        123
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        95,
        99,
        101,
        122,
        123,
        128,
        129,
        138
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        111,
        143
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Shift amount setting",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "The shift amount determines how far the operand is shifted and therefore which result the operation produces. In the serial implementation it also determines how many shift steps are performed.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Changing shamt_i changes the selected barrel-shift stages or the serial count at lines 94 and 128-129, allowing an attacker to produce an incorrect result.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter shamt_i so that the shifter returns a word shifted by an unintended distance.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "shamt_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        94,
        128,
        129
      ],
      "Held Lines": [],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Shift execution control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "This is the control decision that accepts a shift command, selects the supported shift direction and sign behavior, and can cancel a serial operation on a trap. The shifter depends on it to decide whether and how the operand is processed.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Altered control fields can select an incorrect operation or prevent loading and processing through valid_cmd at lines 65-68 and 87-101; asserting cpu_trap can clear the serial operation at line 89 and withhold completion.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could change the decoded command or assert the trap control so that a shift is skipped, canceled, or performed with the wrong behavior.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu",
        "ctrl_i.cpu_trap",
        "ctrl_i.ir_funct12",
        "ctrl_i.ir_funct3"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        65,
        66,
        67,
        68,
        89,
        98,
        101,
        122,
        123,
        143
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        65
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Shift completion and result-valid status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "This status indicates when the requested shift has completed and res_o may be consumed. It is generated inside the unit and leaves through valid_o; it has no separate input port because it is derived from the command and internal sequencing state.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Incorrect valid_o timing or value could cause an integrator to consume an invalid result, while suppressing it can block the result transfer; valid_o is assigned at lines 110 and 144.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could spoof or suppress valid_o so that an incorrect result is accepted or a completed shift is never accepted.",
      "Enters Through": [],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "valid_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [],
      "Held Lines": [
        110,
        144
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        110,
        144
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset behavior",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "Clock and reset inputs and the reset paths they drive are barred from being conceptual assets by the clock and reset rule."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "FAST_SHIFT_EN implementation choice",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "FAST_SHIFT_EN is a build-time generic that selects the implementation and cannot be changed or withheld at run time."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Serial sequencing state and step count",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "shifter.busy, shifter.cnt, shifter.run, shifter.done, and shifter.done_ff only sequence, time, or terminate a shift and are barred by the sequencing-state and status-copy rules."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Barrel-shifter intermediate values",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Serial shift-register intermediate values",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Instruction operation selector as a separate piece",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C3",
      "Why Not Kept": ""
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Unused control-bus information",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The remaining ctrl_i fields are not read or used in this unit, so the RTL shows no mechanism by which they are used, produced, or protected here."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The input word being shifted and the resulting shifted word are one data piece because the same shift operation transforms and returns it. The shifter's operation depends on this word, which enters through rs1_i and leaves through res_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The word can be exposed at res_o through lines 111 and 143, and its value can be altered by the internal data paths at lines 95, 99-101, 122, 128-129, 138, and 143.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe res_o or tamper with the operand or shift datapath so that the returned word reveals data or is incorrect.

conceptual assets.information: The shift amount determines how far the operand is shifted and therefore which result the operation produces. In the serial implementation it also determines how many shift steps are performed.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing shamt_i changes the selected barrel-shift stages or the serial count at lines 94 and 128-129, allowing an attacker to produce an incorrect result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter shamt_i so that the shifter returns a word shifted by an unintended distance.

conceptual assets.information: This is the control decision that accepts a shift command, selects the supported shift direction and sign behavior, and can cancel a serial operation on a trap. The shifter depends on it to decide whether and how the operand is processed.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Altered control fields can select an incorrect operation or prevent loading and processing through valid_cmd at lines 65-68 and 87-101; asserting cpu_trap can clear the serial operation at line 89 and withhold completion.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change the decoded command or assert the trap control so that a shift is skipped, canceled, or performed with the wrong behavior.

conceptual assets.information: This status indicates when the requested shift has completed and res_o may be consumed. It is generated inside the unit and leaves through valid_o; it has no separate input port because it is derived from the command and internal sequencing state.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Incorrect valid_o timing or value could cause an integrator to consume an invalid result, while suppressing it can block the result transfer; valid_o is assigned at lines 110 and 144.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could spoof or suppress valid_o so that an incorrect result is accepted or a completed shift is never accepted.
